content:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., >0.2), model underreacts; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 units per day.
- Model underestimates true price rise when sentiment is weakly positive (0.0–0.2) and history shows upward momentum; add 0.5–1.0 unit bias to forecast.
- Forecast lags in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; shift forecast up 0.3–0.8 units to align with sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.2–0.5 unit downward bias after 5–7 days of flat or declining price.
